fatal_errors: The central hypothesis predicts sluggish diffusion and enhanced thermal stability, opposite to the observed active diffusion, segregation, evaporation, and poor stability.
The proposed inert-gas annealing conditions do not reconstruct the vacuum in situ heating experiment.
The material composition, sub-10 nm size regime, initial FCC multi-twinned/icosahedral structure, and shape dependence are omitted.
explanation: The response addresses the general topic and gives a nominally falsifiable comparison, but it largely restates the conventional entropy-stabilization expectation that the target study disproves. It misses the governing role of surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, shape-enhanced diffusion, shell melting and evaporation, and kinetic rather than entropic control. Its predicted grain retention and compositional stability conflict with the observed loss of 2–4 nm particles, Au/Cu depletion, shape evolution, broader size distribution, and approximately 22% size reduction at 973 K. The conventional-alloy comparison also cannot cleanly distinguish configurational-disorder effects from composition, size, morphology, or surface-energy effects.
